Compare fits on several grids (sensitivity analysis)

Source: R/grid-comparison.R
compare_efron_grids.Rd

compare_efron_grids() fits the model on several grids and returns a table that compares the fits. The range of the grid, the number of grid points, the type of component and the number of spline functions are choices of the analyst, and the table shows how sensitive the results are to these choices. The model is fitted once for each combination of the specified values, called a specification. For each specification, the table contains the posterior mean of the standard deviation of \(g\), the posterior means of a few sites, sampler and grid diagnostics, and elpd_loo, the expected log predictive density for a new site estimated by leave-one-out cross-validation (see loo.bef_fit()).

Usage

compare_efron_grids(
  theta_hat,
  sigma = NULL,
  L = c(51L, 101L, 201L),
  M = c(4L, 6L, 8L),
  expansion = 0.5,
  grid_method = "paper_realdata",
  ...,
  support = NULL,
  component = "point",
  sites = NULL,
  keep_fits = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'bef_grid_comparison'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

theta_hat

Numeric vector of effect estimates, one per site, all on the same scale (e.g., standardized mean differences or log odds ratios). Names, if present, are used as site labels. Can also be a data frame or a bef_data object that contains the estimates and their standard errors (see as_bef_data()), in which case sigma is omitted. At least 5 sites are required.

sigma

Numeric vector of standard errors of the estimates, the same length as theta_hat. All must be positive.

L

Numbers of grid points to compare, a vector of integers from 51 to 401.

M

Numbers of spline functions to compare, a vector of integers from 3 to 10.

expansion

Expansion factors to compare, a numeric vector with values between 0 and 5. See the expansion argument of make_efron_grid().

grid_method

Methods for choosing the limits of the grid, a character vector with one or more of the methods listed in the Details of make_efron_grid(). The default is "paper_realdata", not "pilot" as in bayes_efron_fit(), so that expansion determines the range directly.

...

Further arguments passed to bayes_efron_fit() for every fit, e.g., chains, iter_sampling or seed. Not used by the print() method.

support

Numeric vector of length 2 with the lower and upper limits of the grid, or a list of such vectors to compare several ranges. If support is specified, grid_method and expansion are not used.

component

One or both of "point" (the default) and "normal", the types of component to compare.

sites

Sites whose posterior means are reported, specified as a numeric vector of positions in the data or as a character vector of site labels. If NULL (the default), the sites with the smallest and the largest estimates are used.

keep_fits

If TRUE, the fitted objects are stored in the fits attribute of the result.

x

A bef_grid_comparison object returned by compare_efron_grids().

Value

A data frame of class bef_grid_comparison with one row per specification, sorted by decreasing elpd_loo (best first), and the following columns.

spec

The number of the specification, in the order in which the specifications were fitted.

L, M, expansion, grid_method, component

The settings of the specification.

lower, upper

The lower and upper limits of the grid.

elpd_loo

The expected log predictive density, estimated by leave-one-out cross-validation.

se_elpd_loo

The standard error of elpd_loo.

p_loo

The effective number of parameters as defined by the loo package. This is not the effective_params of a fit.

elpd_diff

The difference in elpd_loo from the first row.

se_diff

The standard error of elpd_diff.

mean_g

The posterior mean of the mean of \(g\).

sd_g

The posterior mean of the standard deviation of \(g\).

site_<label>

The posterior mean of the effect of a selected site, one column per site, named after the site label (e.g., site_4).

max_rhat

The largest R-hat of the fit.

min_ess_bulk

The smallest bulk effective sample size.

divergences

The number of divergent transitions.

max_pareto_k

The largest Pareto k.

end_mass

The largest posterior mass that any site has in the outer 2% of the range at one end of the grid (see Details).

adequate

TRUE if the grid is fine enough for the data (see Details).

sampler_seconds

The sampling time in seconds.

The attribute g is a list, named by spec, with the density of \(g\) for each specification as returned by g_summary(). The attribute sites is a data frame with the rows of site_summary() for the selected sites and a spec column. With keep_fits = TRUE, the attribute fits contains the fitted objects.

Details

The column sd_g and the site columns show how the estimate of \(g\) and the site effects change with the grid. By default the site columns are for the sites with the smallest and the largest estimates, which are the sites that a change of the grid affects most. To vary only how far the grid extends beyond the estimates, specify several values of expansion and a single value each for L and M.

The rows are sorted by elpd_loo, with the largest value first. elpd_diff is the difference in elpd_loo from the first row, and se_diff is the standard error of this difference. A difference of less than about 2 standard errors is not enough to distinguish two specifications, which is the usual case when there are few sites. Note that elpd_loo measures how well a fit predicts the estimate of a new site, and this is hardly affected by the limits of the grid. For example, in the comparison of three ranges for raudenbush1985 that is loaded in the examples, no fit differs from the best by 2 standard errors, although the posterior mean of the study with the largest estimate (column site_4) is much lower with the widest range than with the narrowest. print() adds a note if no specification can be distinguished from the best one.

A fit that has not converged should not be selected for its elpd_loo. Each row therefore includes the largest R-hat, the smallest bulk effective sample size, the number of divergent transitions and the largest Pareto k of its fit. print() lists the rows with an R-hat above 1.05, a divergent transition or a Pareto k above 0.7.

Two more columns check the grid of each fit. end_mass is the largest posterior mass that any site has in the outer 2% of the range at one end of the grid, that is, at its lower or upper limit, as reported by diagnose(). A value above 0.05 means that the result for that site depends on the limits of the grid. adequate is TRUE if the grid is fine enough for the data, as defined in the Details of make_efron_grid(). Warnings from the individual fits are suppressed.

With the default arguments, 9 models are fitted. Each fit uses the default sampler settings of bayes_efron_fit() unless others are specified through .... A message is shown as each fit starts (in these messages, "rule" means the grid method). If a fit fails, a warning is issued and its row has missing values, but the remaining fits are still run. The function requires the loo package.

See also

plot.bef_grid_comparison(), loo.bef_fit(), make_efron_grid(), diagnose(), vignette("choosing-a-grid")

Examples

# Both need CmdStan.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Nine fits of the firm-level callback gaps.
compare_efron_grids(krw_discrimination, seed = 20250807)

# How far the grid extends beyond the estimates, for the 19 studies.
compare_efron_grids(raudenbush1985, L = 101, M = 6,
                    expansion = c(0.25, 0.5, 1), sites = c(4, 8),
                    seed = 1985)
} # }

# The result of the second call is stored with the package.
comparison <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "raudenbush_ranges.rds",
                                  package = "bayesEfron"))
comparison
#> <bef_grid_comparison> 3 specifications, best first
#> 
#> In every row: grid_method = paper_realdata, component = point, L = 101, M = 6
#> 
#>  expansion  lower upper elpd_loo se_elpd_loo elpd_diff se_diff mean_g  sd_g
#>       0.50 -1.070  1.93    -5.22        4.38     0.000   0.000  0.118 0.314
#>       0.25 -0.695  1.56    -5.35        4.18    -0.127   0.300  0.136 0.317
#>       1.00 -1.820  2.68    -5.72        4.22    -0.494   0.537  0.110 0.297
#>  site_4  site_8 max_rhat divergences max_pareto_k end_mass adequate
#>   0.663 -0.0802     1.00           0        0.142 1.35e-02     TRUE
#>   0.782 -0.0792     1.01          18        0.216 5.62e-02     TRUE
#>   0.442 -0.1050     1.00           0        0.276 2.66e-05    FALSE
#> 
#> Rows with convergence or PSIS problems: 2 
#> A specification that did not converge should not be selected on elpd_loo alone.
#> 
#> Rows in which a site has more than 5% of its posterior in the outer 2% of the grid: 2 
#> 
#> elpd_loo does not separate these specifications: all are within two standard 
#> errors of the best. Compare sd_g and the site columns.
plot(comparison)
